FINAL_method: UMA-s-1p1 (omat) Langevin NVT MD; D from Li MSD = 6 D t on window 2-50 ps (msd_origin default); 3-pt Arrhenius (600/800/1000 K); Nernst-Einstein sigma = n q^2 D / (kB T), Haven ratio = 1. This window/pipeline reproduces the validated deck slide for modelc EXACTLY (D 7.90/2.05/4.55e-6, Ea 0.2235, sigma300 13.94 vs slide 14).

modelc_LPSCl1.6.validated: EXACT match to deck slide (msd_origin), Ea 0.2235, sigma300 13.94

comparison.Ea_verdict: b2o3 and modelc have IDENTICAL Ea (0.223 eV) at the consistent 2-50 ps window. The transport gain is NOT a lower barrier.
comparison.verdict: B2O3 doping raises Li conductivity by ~1.33x vs LPSCl1.6 at RT, driven entirely by the prefactor D0 (more carriers / higher attempt rate), at the SAME activation energy. sigma300 18.5 vs 13.9 mS/cm; sigma273 8.7 vs 6.5 mS/cm.

honesty.absolute_sigma: UMA classical Nernst-Einstein (Haven=1) overestimates absolute sigma ~3-5x for the LPSCl family (deck note) -> quote Ea + ratio, not absolute sigma.
honesty.fitting_sensitivity: D from MSD swings ~10-20% with the fit window; this amplifies in the RT extrapolation. The window MUST be held fixed across systems (here 2-50 ps). The earlier (5-40 ps) extraction made modelc 800 K anomalously low -> inflated modelc Ea to 0.226 and faked a b2o3 Ea advantage (0.207). Corrected here.
honesty.comp1_LPSCl_baseline: comp1 columns in msd_comp1_modelc.csv are a DIFFERENT (slower) trajectory than the deck comp1 and do NOT reproduce the slide (D ~60% of slide). Use the deck-validated comp1 reference (D 3.09/1.03e-5/2.20e-5, Ea 0.2532, sigma300 3.35) for the LPSCl baseline.
